symptoms: Leaves have olive-green to brown spots.
Spots are round and velvety with fringed edges.
Older spots turn dark brown to black and grow together.
Leaves with many spots turn yellow and drop by mid-summer.
treatment: Rake up and remove fallen leaves: infected leaves are the source of next year's infection.
Fungicide does not help a tree that is already infected this year. On trees with a history of severe scab, start spraying the following spring at the half-inch green tip stage.
Captan, lime-sulfur and powdered or wettable sulfur are used for control.
prevention: Space trees properly and prune so air moves through the canopy.
apple___Apple_scab.severity: Losing leaves many years in a row weakens the tree.

sources.title: Apple scab of apples and crabapples, University of Minnesota Extension

symptoms: Leaves develop circular spots with purplish or reddish edges and light tan centres.
Large brown rotten areas appear on the fruit, mostly at the blossom end, with brown to black rings on larger infections.
Branches show cankers: sunken, reddish-brown areas.
treatment: Prune out dead or diseased branches.
Remove mummified fruit from the tree.
Fungicides are not recommended unless sanitation and tree care fail to manage the disease.
prevention: Remove infected material from the area.
Prune properly and at the right time of year.
Keep trees healthy with adequate water, and manage fire blight.
Remove the stumps of cut trees, which can be a source of spores.

sources.title: Black rot of apple, University of Minnesota Extension

apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungus (cedar-apple rust), which needs both apple and juniper or red cedar to complete its life cycle
symptoms: Leaf spots are yellow at first, then turn bright orange-red, often with a bright red border.
Small raised black dots form in the centre of mature spots on the upper leaf surface.
Very short finger-like tubes stick out from the underside of the leaf, directly below the spots.
Rarely, green to brown irregular spots with black dots form on the fruit.
treatment: Leaf spots can usually be tolerated: the disease does not significantly affect the tree's overall health.
In late winter or early spring, inspect nearby junipers and red cedars and prune out the brown woody galls before they produce orange structures.
Prune out infected twigs or branches on the apple tree if they occur.
prevention: Do not plant eastern red cedar or junipers within a few hundred yards of susceptible apple trees.
apple___Cedar_apple_rust.severity: Damages the leaves and fruit of very susceptible apple varieties, but is only a minor problem on resistant or partly resistant trees.

sources.title: Cedar-apple rust and related rust diseases, University of Minnesota Extension
